extractedFacts.premisesPunitiveDamagesStandard: Clear and Convincing Evidence -- Ohio Rev. Code § 2315.21(D)(4)
extractedFacts.premisesPunitiveDamagesCap: For an individual or 'small employer' defendant: the LESSER of 2x compensatory damages or 10% of the defendant's net worth at the time of the tort, capped at $350,000 -- Ohio Rev. Code § 2315.21(D)(2)(a). A separate, differently-structured limit applies to larger employers.
extractedFacts.premisesOpenAndObviousCitation: Armstrong v. Best Buy Co., 99 Ohio St.3d 79, 2003-Ohio-2573, 788 N.E.2d 1088 (Ohio 2003)
extractedFacts.premisesNegligentSecurityCitation: Simpson v. Big Bear Stores Co., 73 Ohio St.3d 130, 652 N.E.2d 702 (Ohio 1995)
extractedFacts.premisesModeOfOperationCitation: Johnson v. Wagner Provision Co., 141 Ohio St. 584, 49 N.E.2d 925 (Ohio 1943) (self-service exception to the notice requirement)
extractedFacts.premisesLiabilityDistinctNote: Ohio does not recognize a Texas-style bright-line distinction between a premises-condition claim and an ordinary-negligence/activity claim. Premises liability in Ohio is simply negligence law overlaid with the invitee/licensee/trespasser duty framework, not a separate cause of action.

outcome.description: The jury found the operator negligent and on February 12, 2024 awarded the claimant $1,300,000 in noneconomic damages; the trial court denied the operator's motion for JNOV or new trial. The Eighth District reversed on March 13, 2025, holding there was no evidence of constructive notice of the liquid, and reversed the denial of JNOV, which leaves the claimant with nothing; the operator's argument that Ohio's noneconomic-damages cap should have been applied was not reached. No later Ohio Supreme Court merits opinion appears in the Reporter of Decisions. No attorney's fees.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed: JNOV should have been granted for the restaurant operator.
